name: Ines Varga
headline: Revenue operations for Series A and Series B software companies | Forecasting you can take to the board, CRM migration without a lost quarter | Fractional RevOps lead, ex-Tallowmere Systems
about:
Most Series B forecasts are a spreadsheet one person understands. I rebuild revenue operations so the number sales leaders give the board on day 5 is the number they close on day 90.

I work with B2B software companies between roughly 30 and 200 people, usually in the year after a funding round, when the CRM that worked for six sellers stops working for thirty.

What that has looked like:
- At Tallowmere Systems I led a CRM migration covering 62 sellers and 4 years of pipeline history. We cut over in one weekend and lost no open opportunities.
- The forecasting process I introduced brought quarterly forecast error from 31% to 9% across 6 consecutive quarters.
- At Brightquay Logistics I redesigned territories and commission for 40 sellers; disputes per quarter fell from 22 to 3.

How I work: a three-week diagnostic first, written up in plain language, then a fixed-scope rebuild with your team doing the work alongside me so it survives after I leave.

I take on two clients at a time. If your forecast and your CRM disagree, send me a message with your team size and CRM, and I will tell you within a day whether I can help.
